**A watermark adds a small statistical preference that a detector knows how to look for.** A secret, context-dependent rule divides candidate tokens into favored and unfavored groups. Generation slightly prefers the favored group, leaving a detectable excess over many tokens. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.10226)

In a simplified null model with favored fraction gamma, T tokens have expected favored count gamma times T and standard deviation $\sqrt{T\gamma(1-\gamma)}$. The standardized excess is a z-score. Longer text can provide more statistical power under the model assumptions.

**Text is not a sequence of perfectly independent coin flips.** Repetition, low-entropy passages, editing, and mixed authorship affect the test. Paraphrasing can weaken the signal, and repeated testing changes false-positive considerations.

Calibrate thresholds on relevant human and generated text. A positive result is evidence for a particular keyed watermark mechanism, not universal proof of AI authorship. An absent watermark does not establish human origin. Protect the key and communicate uncertainty; a detector's statistical output should not be treated as an infallible identity or provenance certificate.

**Technical details and references.**

A token watermark uses a secret, context-dependent partition of vocabulary into favored and unfavored tokens, then biases generation toward the favored set. A detector counts favored tokens and compares with the null expectation. In a simplified independent null with favored fraction $\gamma$, $z=(G-\gamma T)/\sqrt{T\gamma(1-\gamma)}$. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.10226)

Real text violates simple independence assumptions, and detection power depends on length, entropy, edits, and the chosen key. Paraphrasing or mixed authorship can reduce the signal; repeated testing needs calibrated thresholds. A positive score is statistical evidence for a particular watermarking mechanism, not proof of authorship or a universal AI-text detector. Validate false positives on relevant human text and protect keys; do not equate missing watermark evidence with human origin.
